title: The same SN2 again, with the sodium counterion quietly reduced from a cation to a sodium atom behind a well written spectator declaration

expect.note: This is assertion 5 of conservation-spectator-declaration, the attack. The declaration is well formed: the species is present in both states, declared once in each, justified, and owned. The participating members balance perfectly on mass, charge, and valence electrons, so the other conservation checks see a clean SN2. Put the spectator back and the step falls apart, because sodium is a cation on the left and a neutral sodium atom with one unpaired electron on the right. A one electron reduction of sodium in the middle of a bromide displacement is chemically absurd, and the whole point is that the exclusion is what makes the step look balanced. Two violations from this check: the spectator is not structurally identical across the step, and with spectators counted the totals move by one unit of charge and one valence electron. Every atom passes valence on its own terms, since Na+ with nothing on it derives +1 and a sodium atom with one unpaired electron derives 0. conservation-electron-flow is declared because observedDeltas walks all members, spectators included, so it sees the nonbonding electron appear on sodium with no arrow claiming it. That is the correct behaviour and it is why the deltas half of the family is not fooled by a spectator declaration even though the totals half is.

spectators.justification: Sodium balances the bromide charge and takes no part in the displacement, so it is excluded from the totals on both sides.
